newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand acts on high rice, fertiliser prices.
newsitem.headline: Thailand acts on high rice, fertiliser prices.

text.p: Thai commerce minister Narongchai Akrasanee said on Monday he would adopt measures to halt a sharp increase in rice and fertiliser prices in the past several weeks.

"The most pressing issue now is the steep rise of rice and fertiliser prices. The ministry this week plans to help ease local rice prices by selling it cheaper from government inventory," Narongchai told reporters.

Retail rice prices have risen substantially in the past two weeks as Thai housewives scrambled to hoard the staple on concern that a new 10-percent value added tax (VAT) from last Saturday would push up prices.
But the ministry said rice was not subject to VAT.

Narongchai said he will also have discussions with fertiliser importers to seek cooperation for easing scarcity and high prices of the commodity after the baht's de facto devaluation in early July. The baht has lost almost 25 percent of its value since then.
